reasoning_content:
Both were restarted. Next, let's wait for the ready state. Note: these have now been restarted multiple times across multiple waves. The pattern (batch SIGTERM during the parallel startup wave, then clean exit, process-compose marks it as "aborted, won't become ready" so no auto-restart) is due to memory pressure during the initial parallel startup of about 38 processes in a 7.6GB environment.

Let's poll for ready state and check memory.

action.command:
sleep 75; cd /workspace
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  a=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 2 http://localhost:18006/docs 2>/dev/null)
  b=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 2 http://localhost:18014/docs 2>/dev/null)
  echo "poll $i: objections=$a codec=$b mem=$(free -h | awk 'NR==2{print $3" used"}')"
  [ "$a" = "200" ] && [ "$b" = "200" ] && break
  sleep 30
done

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments:
{"command": "sleep 75; cd /workspace
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  a=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 2 http://localhost:18006/docs 2>/dev/null)
  b=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -m 2 http://localhost:18014/docs 2>/dev/null)
  echo "poll $i: objections=$a codec=$b mem=$(free -h | awk 'NR==2{print $3" used"}')"
  [ "$a" = "200" ] && [ "$b" = "200" ] && break
  sleep 30
done", "summary": "Poll restarted services until ready"}
